newsitem.title: NIGER: President's allies head for poll victory in Niger.
newsitem.headline: President's allies head for poll victory in Niger.

text.p: The political party allied with Niger's President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara headed for an easy victory with results declared on Sunday for more than two-thirds of seats in legislative elections boycotted by the opposition.

The Independent Elections Committee put average turnout in voting on Saturday at only 27.32 percent, confirming the impact of a boycott by the main opposition parties, who demand a rerun of a chaotic July presidential poll they say was rigged by Mainassara.
The opposition hailed the success of the boycott. Final turnout in July was 66.34 percent.

The Union of Independents for Democratic Renewal won 44 of the assembly's 83 seats from 67 declared by 8 p.m. (1900 GMT). Eight went to the ANDP party with the rest shared by seven minor parties and three independents, a commission statement said.
Political problems since the start of a democratic transition in 1990 have stoked economic decline in one of the poorest countries in Sub-Saharan Africa.
A series a strikes over the past year linked to the political crisis spread at some point to Niger's lifeblood uranium mining industry, already depressed by low world prices.
A total of 220 candidates from a dozen small parties sought seats. Around 3.8 million people were eligible to vote.
Mainassara, a coup maker who legalised his rule through the disputed July election, had urged a huge turnout and expressed regret that the opposition was not taking part.
"The low turnout shows Niger cannot be governed without the opposition," leading opposition politician Bello Tiousso Garba told Reuters.
Mainassara ousted the elected government of civilian president Mahamane Ousmane in a coup last January following a long standoff between Ousmane and his prime minister.

The general offered himself for election in July, but then suspended the electoral commission on the second day of polling, accusing it of irregularities, and placed his opponents under house arrest. He appointed a new commission which declared him winner with 52.22 percent of votes cast.
The United States said the election was fraudulent and suspended development aid.
Opposition politicians, including Ousmane, refused to register for Saturday's poll demanding that the result of the July presidential election be scrapped.
Final provisional results were expected sometime on Sunday but these would have to be verified by the Supreme Court.
